correctness.rationale: After an edge-selection prefix in the underlying complete graph, the undominated vertices of its line graph are exactly edges among unused ground vertices plus isolated selected-edge components. Distinguishing A,B0,B1,C1,C2 legal moves yields conservation L=n-u-b1-c2; a completed sequence has u in {0,1}, and the transition to a first nontrivial component forces L<=n-1, with equality only odd n and near-perfect-matching/attachment structure. Explicit even construction attains n-2; rooted contracted-tree order realizes each odd support. Matching and attachment choices count n!(n-1)!/2^m without overcounting ordered sequences. Independently computed open-neighborhood bitset dynamic-programming maximum length and number for n=3..8, yielding odd counts 6,720,453600 and matching length at each n; finite DP is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The maximal legal open-neighborhood domination length and complete equality-pattern/ordered census are natural structural invariants of a highly symmetric graph family, not a short parameter substitution. The matching-to-spanning-tree support bijection supplies a useful combinatorial characterization beyond a scalar maximum.

final_claim: For T_n=L(K_n), n>=3, the open-neighborhood Grundy total domination number is n-1 for odd n and n-2 for even n. Every maximum odd-order ordered sequence first selects a near-perfect matching then joins the unmatched vertex and attaches each remaining matched pair one at a time. For n=2m+1 the number of labelled ordered longest sequences is (2m+1)!(2m)!/2^m, and their unordered supports are exactly the spanning trees containing a matching of size m.
limitations: No enumeration of even-order ordered maxima or number of distinct trees is claimed.
The near-perfect matching need not be a graph automorphism quotient; all orders and labels count.
Finite n<=8 code corroborates but does not prove the all-n move classification.
